rows.reasoning: At x=2, rationalizing (sqrt(x+2)-2)/(x-2) gives 1/(sqrt(x+2)+2), whose limit is 1/4, not 1/2. The other four limits are 8, 3, 0, and 2.
f(x)=x^2(1+o(1)) and g(x)=x(2+o(1)); dividing numerator and denominator by x gives (x(1+o(1))+1)/(2+o(1)+1) -> 1/3, choice 5.
Continuity at 3 requires 12-3m=0, so m=4. Then the quotient is x-1 near 3, so n=2 and m+n=6, choice 4.
For x not 2, f(x)=(sqrt(x-1)-1)/(x-2)=1/(sqrt(x-1)+1). Continuity gives f(2)=1/2, choice 1.
For x!=2, f(x)=x+5. Differentiability at 2 requires the assigned value m+1 to equal the limit 7, so m=6, choice 3.
Continuity gives 1-2k=k-5, hence k=2 and f(0)=1-2k=-3. Thus k+f(0)=-1, choice 2.
The derivative of x^2-x+5 is 2x-1. Slope 1 occurs at x=1, where y=5; the tangent is y=x+4, choice 4.
The secant slope on [1,2] is (-5-0)/(2-1)=-5. Solving f'(c)=-4c+1=-5 gives c=3/2, choice 3.

Only ㄱ is always true by subtracting the two existing limits. ㄴ fails without continuity of g at the limit of f; ㄷ may have a zero limiting denominator; ㄹ fails for f=g=sin(1/(x-a)), whose difference is identically zero. Therefore ㄱ only, choice 1.
The quotient tends to 2f'(1), so f'(1)=3. Since f'(1)=3+2m-4=2m-1, m=2.
Differentiate the identity with respect to y and set y=0: f'(x)=f'(0)+6x=4+6x, choice 4.
The derivative 3(x-1)^2 equals 3 at x=0 and 2, producing parallel tangent lines y=3x+1 and y=3x-3. Their distance is 4/sqrt(10), choice 2.

The graph’s secant from x=-2 to x=4 has negative slope. A horizontal-derivative level equal to that negative slope occurs once on the initial decreasing branch and twice on the descending branch after the interior maximum, for 3 values of c, choice 3.
A right shift gives g(x)=f(x-p). The limits force f(0)=f'(0)=0 and f(-p)=0; with monic cubic f(x)=x^2(x+p). The first limit is 1/p=p, so p=1; then g(2)=f(1)=2, choice 1.
The intersection count changes at the distance 12/5 from O to hypotenuse AB, and at vertex radii OB=3 and OA=4. Their sum is 12/5+3+4=47/5, choice 4.

For |f-p| to be differentiable across the sign change from +infinity to -infinity, the crossing must occur at the smooth join with zero derivative: a=2 and f(-1)=p. Thus f=p+(x+1)^2 on x<=-1 and f=p-(x+1)^2 on x>-1. Its unique simple zero is q=sqrt(p)-1. From f(p)=-p(p+1)=-21, p=4, so q=1 and f'(q)=-2(q+1)=-4, choice 4.

Finite asymptotic limit forces f=x^2+ax+b with integers a,b. The limit is a and f(-4)=16-4a+b, giving b=5a-16. Continuity of x/f(x) on all reals requires f to have no real zero; its discriminant a^2-20a+64=(a-4)(a-16) must be negative, hence a=5,...,15. Then f(2)=7a-12 has min 23 and max 93, whose sum is 116.

P on the curve gives f(1)=-2. The derivative of (x^2-3)f(x) at 1 is 2, so the tangent is y=2x+2. The circle center lies on the normal through P, (1,4)+t(-2,1), with radius sqrt(5)|t|. Tangency to the x-axis requires center y=radius. The first-quadrant solution is t=1-sqrt(5), radius=5-sqrt(5); area=pi(5-sqrt(5))^2=(30-10sqrt(5))*pi.
